sanskrit: jaghanaṃ pālayām āsa virāṭaḥ saha kekayaiḥ kāśirājaś ca śaibyaś ca rathānām ayutais tribhiḥ
english: Virāṭa, together with the Kekayas, guarded the rear, as did the king of Kāśi and Śaibya, with thirty thousand chariots.

sanskrit: evam etaṃ mahāvyūhaṃ vyūhya bhārata pāṇḍavāḥ sūryodayanam icchantaḥ sthitā yuddhāya daṃśitāḥ
english: Having marshalled this great battle-array, O Bhārata, the Pāṇḍavas, armoured and longing for the sunrise, stood ready for battle.

sanskrit: teṣām ādityavarṇāni vimalāni mahānti ca śvetacchatrāṇy aśobhanta vāraṇeṣu ratheṣu ca
english: Sun-coloured, spotless, and vast, their white parasols shone resplendent upon the elephants and the chariots.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca krauñcaṃ tato mahāvyūham abhedyaṃ tanayas tava vyūḍhaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāghoraṃ pārthenāmitatejasā
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, beholding the great Krauñca formation—impenetrable and most terrible—drawn up by Pārtha of immeasurable splendour, your son,

sanskrit: ācāryam upasaṃgamya kṛpaṃ śalyaṃ ca māriṣa saumadattiṃ vikarṇaṃ ca aśvatthāmānam eva ca
english: approaching the preceptor, O venerable one, and Kṛpa and Śalya, and the son of Somadatta and Vikarṇa, and Aśvatthāman as well,

sanskrit: duḥśāsanādīn bhrātṝṃś ca sa sarvān eva bhārata anyāṃś ca subahūñ śūrān yuddhāya samupāgatān
english: and Duḥśāsana and his other brothers, all of them, O Bhārata, and the many other heroes who had assembled for battle,

sanskrit: prāhedaṃ vacanaṃ kāle harṣayaṃs tanayas tava nānāśastrapraharaṇāḥ sarve śastrāstravedinaḥ
english: your son, gladdening them, spoke these timely words: "All of you wield manifold weapons and are versed in arms and missiles.

sanskrit: ekaikaśaḥ samarthā hi yūyaṃ sarve mahārathāḥ pāṇḍuputrān raṇe hantuṃ sasainyān kim u saṃhatāḥ
english: Each one of you, all great chariot-warriors, is alone able to slay the sons of Pāṇḍu with their host in battle—how much more so when united!

sanskrit: aparyāptaṃ tad asmākaṃ balaṃ bhīṣmābhirakṣitam paryāptaṃ tv idam eteṣāṃ balaṃ pārthivasattamāḥ
english: Unlimited is this our force, guarded by Bhīṣma, while limited is this force of theirs, O best of kings.

sanskrit: saṃsthānāḥ śūrasenāś ca veṇikāḥ kukurās tathā ārevakās trigartāś ca madrakā yavanās tathā
english: Let the Saṃsthānas and the Śūrasenas, the Veṇikas and the Kukuras, the Ārevakas and the Trigartas, the Madrakas and the Yavanas,

sanskrit: śatruṃjayena sahitās tathā duḥśāsanena ca vikarṇena ca vīreṇa tathā nandopanandakaiḥ
english: together with Śatruṃjaya and with Duḥśāsana, and with the heroic Vikarṇa, and with Nanda and Upananda,

sanskrit: citrasenena sahitāḥ sahitāḥ pāṇibhadrakaiḥ bhīṣmam evābhirakṣantu saha sainyapuraskṛtāḥ
english: joined with Citrasena and with the Pāṇibhadrakas, set their armies before them and guard Bhīṣma above all."

sanskrit: tato droṇaś ca bhīṣmaś ca tava putraś ca māriṣa avyūhanta mahāvyūhaṃ pāṇḍūnāṃ pratibādhane
english: Then Droṇa and Bhīṣma and your son, O venerable one, drew up a great formation to repel the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: bhīṣmaḥ sainyena mahatā samantāt parivāritaḥ yayau prakarṣan mahatīṃ vāhinīṃ surarāḍ iva
english: Bhīṣma, surrounded on every side by a mighty host, advanced, leading on the great army like the king of the gods.

sanskrit: tam anvayān maheṣvāso bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān kuntalaiś ca daśārṇaiś ca māgadhaiś ca viśāṃ pate
english: Behind him followed the mighty archer, the valorous son of Bharadvāja, with the Kuntalas and the Daśārṇas and the Māgadhas, O lord of peoples,

sanskrit: vidarbhair mekalaiś caiva karṇaprāvaraṇair api sahitāḥ sarvasainyena bhīṣmam āhavaśobhinam
english: with the Vidarbhas and the Mekalas and the Karṇaprāvaraṇas as well, together with the whole army, behind Bhīṣma resplendent in battle.

sanskrit: gāndhārāḥ sindhusauvīrāḥ śibayo 'tha vasātayaḥ śakuniś ca svasainyena bhāradvājam apālayat
english: The Gāndhāras, the Sindhus and Sauvīras, the Śibis, and then the Vasātis—and Śakuni with his own troops—guarded the son of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā sahitaḥ sarvasodaraiḥ aśvātakair vikarṇaiś ca tathā śarmilakosalaiḥ
english: Then King Duryodhana, together with all his brothers, with the Aśvātakas and the Vikarṇas, and likewise with the Śarmilas and the Kosalas,

sanskrit: daradaiś cūcupaiś caiva tathā kṣudrakamālavaiḥ abhyarakṣata saṃhṛṣṭaḥ saubaleyasya vāhinīm
english: and with the Daradas and the Cūcupas, and likewise the Kṣudrakas and the Mālavas, joyfully guarded the host of Subala's son.

sanskrit: bhūriśravāḥ śalaḥ śalyo bhagadattaś ca māriṣa vindānuvindāv āvantyau vāmaṃ pārśvam apālayan
english: Bhūriśravas, Śala, Śalya, and Bhagadatta, O venerable one, and Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, guarded the left flank.

sanskrit: saumadattiḥ suśarmā ca kāmbojaś ca sudakṣiṇaḥ śatāyuś ca śrutāyuś ca dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvam āsthitāḥ
english: The son of Somadatta and Suśarman, and Sudakṣiṇa the Kāmboja, and Śatāyus and Śrutāyus, took their place on the right flank.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā kṛpaś caiva kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ mahatyā senayā sārdhaṃ senāpṛṣṭhe vyavasthitāḥ
english: Aśvatthāman and Kṛpa, and Kṛtavarman of the Sātvata line, with a great army stationed themselves at the rear of the host.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhagopās tu tasyāsan nānādeśyā janeśvarāḥ ketumān vasudānaś ca putraḥ kāśyasya cābhibhūḥ
english: The guardians of its rear were kings from various lands—Ketumat and Vasudāna, and Abhibhū the son of the king of Kāśi.

sanskrit: tatas te tāvakāḥ sarve hṛṣṭā yuddhāya bhārata dadhmuḥ śaṅkhān mudā yuktāḥ siṃhanādāṃś ca nādayan
english: Then all your warriors, rejoicing for battle, O Bhārata, filled with gladness blew their conches and let loose their lion-roars.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ śrutvā tu hṛṣṭānāṃ kuruvṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ siṃhanādaṃ vinadyoccaiḥ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān
english: Hearing the lion-roar of those joyful men, the aged grandsire of the Kurus, the valorous one, roared aloud in answer and blew his conch.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaṅkhāś ca bheryaś ca peśyaś ca vividhāḥ paraiḥ ānakāś cābhyahanyanta sa śabdas tumulo 'bhavat
english: Then conches and kettledrums and tabors of many kinds, and war-drums, were sounded by the foe, and the din became tumultuous.

sanskrit: tataḥ śvetair hayair yukte mahati syandane sthitau pradadhmatuḥ śaṅkhavarau hemaratnapariṣkṛtau
english: Then, stationed upon a great chariot yoked with white horses, the two blew their excellent conches, adorned with gold and gems—

sanskrit: pāñcajanyaṃ hṛṣīkeśo devadattaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ pauṇḍraṃ dadhmau mahāśaṅkhaṃ bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ
english: Hṛṣīkeśa blew the Pāñcajanya, Dhanaṃjaya the Devadatta, and Vṛkodara of terrible deeds blew the great conch Pauṇḍra.

sanskrit: anantavijayaṃ rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca sughoṣamaṇipuṣpakau
english: King Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, blew the Anantavijaya, while Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughoṣa and the Maṇipuṣpaka.

sanskrit: kāśirājaś ca śaibyaś ca śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaś ca sātyakiś ca mahāyaśāḥ
english: The king of Kāśi and Śaibya, and Śikhaṇḍin the great chariot-warrior, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Virāṭa, and Sātyaki of great renown,

sanskrit: pāñcālyaś ca maheṣvāso draupadyāḥ pañca cātmajāḥ sarve dadhmur mahāśaṅkhān siṃhanādāṃś ca nedire
english: and the Pāñcāla prince the mighty archer, and the five sons of Draupadī—all blew their great conches and sounded their lion-roars.

sanskrit: sa ghoṣaḥ sumahāṃs tatra vīrais taiḥ samudīritaḥ nabhaś ca pṛthivīṃ caiva tumulo vyanunādayat
english: That mighty din, raised there by those heroes, tumultuous, made both sky and earth resound.

sanskrit: evam ete mahārāja prahṛṣṭāḥ kurupāṇḍavāḥ punar yuddhāya saṃjagmus tāpayānāḥ parasparam
english: Thus, O great king, the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, exultant, came together once more for battle, tormenting one another.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca evaṃ vyūḍheṣv anīkeṣu māmakeṣv itareṣu ca kathaṃ praharatāṃ śreṣṭhāḥ saṃprahāraṃ pracakrire
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When the armies were thus drawn up, my own and the others, how did those foremost of warriors begin their onslaught?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca samaṃ vyūḍheṣv anīkeṣu saṃnaddhā ruciradhvajāḥ apāram iva saṃdṛśya sāgarapratimaṃ balam
english: Saṃjaya said: When the armies stood evenly arrayed, accoutred and bright with banners, beholding the host like a shoreless ocean,

sanskrit: teṣāṃ madhye sthito rājā putro duryodhanas tava abravīt tāvakān sarvān yudhyadhvam iti daṃśitāḥ
english: in their midst stood King Duryodhana, your son, and said to all your warriors: "Fight, you who are armoured!"

sanskrit: te manaḥ krūram āsthāya samabhityaktajīvitāḥ pāṇḍavān abhyavartanta sarva evocchritadhvajāḥ
english: Hardening their hearts to cruelty, casting away their lives, they all advanced upon the Pāṇḍavas with banners upraised.

sanskrit: tato yuddhaṃ samabhavat tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca vyatiṣaktarathadvipam
english: Then there arose a tumultuous, hair-raising battle between your men and the foe, with chariots and elephants entangled together.

sanskrit: muktās tu rathibhir bāṇā rukmapuṅkhāḥ sutejanāḥ saṃnipetur akuṇṭhāgrā nāgeṣu ca hayeṣu ca
english: Arrows loosed by the chariot-warriors, gold-feathered and keen-edged, with unblunted points, fell upon the elephants and the horses.

sanskrit: tathā pravṛtte saṃgrāme dhanur udyamya daṃśitaḥ abhipatya mahābāhur bhīṣmo bhīmaparākramaḥ
english: As the battle thus raged, the mighty-armed Bhīṣma of terrible prowess, armoured, raised his bow and charged forward.

sanskrit: saubhadre bhīmasene ca śaineye ca mahārathe kekaye ca virāṭe ca dhṛṣṭadyumne ca pārṣate
english: Upon the son of Subhadrā and upon Bhīmasena, upon Śini's grandson the great chariot-warrior, upon Kekaya and Virāṭa, and upon Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata—

sanskrit: eteṣu naravīreṣu cedimatsyeṣu cābhitaḥ vavarṣa śaravarṣāṇi vṛddhaḥ kurupitāmahaḥ
english: upon these heroes among men, and upon the Cedis and Matsyas all around, the aged grandsire of the Kurus rained showers of arrows.

sanskrit: prākampata mahāvyūhas tasmin vīrasamāgame sarveṣām eva sainyānām āsīd vyatikaro mahān
english: The great formation shook in that meeting of heroes, and there was a vast confusion among all the armies.

sanskrit: sāditadhvajanāgāś ca hatapravaravājinaḥ viprayātarathānīkāḥ samapadyanta pāṇḍavāḥ
english: With their banners and elephants cast down, their finest steeds slain, and their ranks of chariots scattered, so the Pāṇḍavas became.

sanskrit: arjunas tu naravyāghro dṛṣṭvā bhīṣmaṃ mahāratham vārṣṇeyam abravīt kruddho yāhi yatra pitāmahaḥ
english: But Arjuna, the tiger among men, seeing Bhīṣma the great chariot-warrior, said in wrath to the Vṛṣṇi hero: "Drive to where the grandsire is.

sanskrit: eṣa bhīṣmaḥ susaṃkruddho vārṣṇeya mama vāhinīm nāśayiṣyati suvyaktaṃ duryodhanahite rataḥ
english: This Bhīṣma, sorely enraged, O Vṛṣṇi hero, will surely destroy my host, intent upon Duryodhana's good.

sanskrit: eṣa droṇaḥ kṛpaḥ śalyo vikarṇaś ca janārdana dhārtarāṣṭrāś ca sahitā duryodhanapurogamāḥ
english: This Droṇa, and Kṛpa, Śalya, and Vikarṇa, O Janārdana, and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra united, with Duryodhana at their head,

sanskrit: pāñcālān nihaniṣyanti rakṣitā dṛḍhadhanvanā so 'haṃ bhīṣmaṃ gamiṣyāmi sainyahetor janārdana
english: will slaughter the Pāñcālas, guarded by that firm-bowed one. Therefore I shall go against Bhīṣma for the sake of the army, O Janārdana."

sanskrit: tam abravīd vāsudevo yatto bhava dhanaṃjaya eṣa tvā prāpaye vīra pitāmaharathaṃ prati
english: To him Vāsudeva said: "Be on your guard, Dhanaṃjaya. I am bringing you, O hero, against the grandsire's chariot."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tataḥ śaurī rathaṃ taṃ lokaviśrutam prāpayām āsa bhīṣmāya rathaṃ prati janeśvara
english: Having spoken thus, the descendant of Śūra brought that world-famed chariot up against Bhīṣma's chariot, O lord of men.

sanskrit: cañcadbahupatākena balākāvarṇavājinā samucchritamahābhīmanadadvānaraketunā mahatā meghanādena rathenādityavarcasā
english: With its many fluttering pennons, with horses the colour of cranes, with its great and most terrible roaring ape-banner upraised, with the mighty thunder of his chariot bright as the sun,

sanskrit: vinighnan kauravānīkaṃ śūrasenāṃś ca pāṇḍavaḥ āyāc charān nudañ śīghraṃ suhṛcchoṣavināśanaḥ
english: the Pāṇḍava, smiting the Kaurava host and the Śūrasenas, came on swiftly, loosing arrows—he who dispels the grief of friends.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ vegena prabhinnam iva vāraṇam trāsayānaṃ raṇe śūrān pātayantaṃ ca sāyakaiḥ
english: As he rushed on with violence like a rutting elephant, terrifying the heroes in battle and felling them with his shafts,

sanskrit: saindhavapramukhair guptaḥ prācyasauvīrakekayaiḥ sahasā pratyudīyāya bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo 'rjunam
english: Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu, guarded by the Saindhava chiefs and by the Easterners, Sauvīras, and Kekayas, suddenly came forth to meet Arjuna.

sanskrit: ko hi gāṇḍīvadhanvānam anyaḥ kurupitāmahāt droṇavaikartanābhyāṃ vā rathaḥ saṃyātum arhati
english: For what chariot-warrior, other than the Kuru grandsire, or Droṇa, or the son of the Sun, was fit to encounter the wielder of Gāṇḍīva?

sanskrit: tato bhīṣmo mahārāja kauravāṇāṃ pitāmahaḥ arjunaṃ saptasaptatyā nārācānāṃ samāvṛṇot
english: Then Bhīṣma, O great king, the grandsire of the Kauravas, covered Arjuna with seventy-seven iron arrows.

sanskrit: droṇaś ca pañcaviṃśatyā kṛpaḥ pañcāśatā śaraiḥ duryodhanaś catuḥṣaṣṭyā śalyaś ca navabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Droṇa pierced him with twenty-five, Kṛpa with fifty arrows, Duryodhana with sixty-four, and Śalya with nine arrows,

sanskrit: saindhavo navabhiś cāpi śakuniś cāpi pañcabhiḥ vikarṇo daśabhir bhallai rājan vivyādha pāṇḍavam
english: and the lord of the Sindhus with nine, and Śakuni too with five, and Vikarṇa with ten broad-headed shafts, O king, pierced the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: sa tair viddho maheṣvāsaḥ samantān niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ na vivyathe mahābāhur bhidyamāna ivācalaḥ
english: Pierced on every side by those whetted arrows, the mighty archer of great arms did not waver, like a mountain being split.

sanskrit: sa bhīṣmaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā kṛpaṃ ca navabhiḥ śaraiḥ droṇaṃ ṣaṣṭyā naravyāghro vikarṇaṃ ca tribhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: That tiger among men, in turn, pierced Bhīṣma with twenty-five arrows and Kṛpa with nine, Droṇa with sixty and Vikarṇa with three arrows,

sanskrit: ārtāyaniṃ tribhir bāṇai rājānaṃ cāpi pañcabhiḥ pratyavidhyad ameyātmā kirīṭī bharatarṣabha
english: and the son of Ṛtāyana with three shafts and the king with five did the diademed one of immeasurable spirit strike back, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: taṃ sātyakir virāṭaś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ draupadeyābhimanyuś ca parivavrur dhanaṃjayam
english: Sātyaki and Virāṭa, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata, and the sons of Draupadī, and Abhimanyu, surrounded Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: tato droṇaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ gāṅgeyasya priye ratam abhyavarṣata pāñcālyaḥ saṃyuktaḥ saha somakaiḥ
english: Then the Pāñcāla prince, joined with the Somakas, rained arrows upon Droṇa the mighty archer, who was intent on the welfare of the son of Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: bhīṣmas tu rathināṃ śreṣṭhas tūrṇaṃ vivyādha pāṇḍavam aśītyā niśitair bāṇais tato 'krośanta tāvakāḥ
english: But Bhīṣma, foremost of chariot-warriors, swiftly pierced the Pāṇḍava with eighty whetted arrows, and at that your men cried out in joy.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu ninadaṃ śrutvā prahṛṣṭānāṃ prahṛṣṭavat praviveśa tato madhyaṃ rathasiṃhaḥ pratāpavān
english: Hearing the clamour of those exultant men, the valorous lion among chariot-warriors, himself exultant, then plunged into their midst.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu rathasiṃhānāṃ madhyaṃ prāpya dhanaṃjayaḥ cikrīḍa dhanuṣā rājaṃl lakṣyaṃ kṛtvā mahārathān
english: Reaching the midst of those lions among chariot-warriors, Dhanaṃjaya sported with his bow, O king, making targets of those great chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā bhīṣmam āha janeśvaraḥ pīḍyamānaṃ svakaṃ sainyaṃ dṛṣṭvā pārthena saṃyuge
english: Then King Duryodhana, the lord of men, seeing his own army hard pressed by Pārtha in the fray, said to Bhīṣma:

sanskrit: eṣa pāṇḍusutas tāta kṛṣṇena sahito balī yatatāṃ sarvasainyānāṃ mūlaṃ naḥ parikṛntati tvayi jīvati gāṅgeye droṇe ca rathināṃ vare
english: "This mighty son of Pāṇḍu, dear sire, joined with Kṛṣṇa, cuts away the very root of our whole striving army, even while you, the son of Gaṅgā, and Droṇa, foremost of chariot-warriors, yet live.

sanskrit: tvatkṛte hy eṣa karṇo 'pi nyastaśastro mahārathaḥ na yudhyati raṇe pārthaṃ hitakāmaḥ sadā mama
english: For on your account even this Karṇa, the great chariot-warrior, has laid down his weapons and does not fight Pārtha in battle, though ever desiring my welfare.

sanskrit: sa tathā kuru gāṅgeya yathā hanyeta phalgunaḥ evam uktas tato rājan pitā devavratas tava dhik kṣatradharmam ity uktvā yayau pārtharathaṃ prati
english: Act, then, O son of Gaṅgā, so that Phalguna may be slain." Thus addressed, O king, your sire Devavrata said, "Shame upon the warrior's code!"—and drove against Pārtha's chariot.

sanskrit: ubhau śvetahayau rājan saṃsaktau dṛśya pārthivāḥ siṃhanādān bhṛśaṃ cakruḥ śaṅkhaśabdāṃś ca bhārata
english: Beholding the two white-horsed warriors locked in combat, O king, the kings raised loud lion-roars and conch-blasts, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: drauṇir duryodhanaś caiva vikarṇaś ca tavātmajaḥ parivārya raṇe bhīṣmaṃ sthitā yuddhāya māriṣa
english: The son of Droṇa, and Duryodhana, and Vikarṇa your son, surrounding Bhīṣma in the battle, stood ready to fight, O venerable one.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavāḥ sarve parivārya dhanaṃjayam sthitā yuddhāya mahate tato yuddham avartata
english: In the same way all the Pāṇḍavas, surrounding Dhanaṃjaya, stood ready for the great battle; and then the fight began.

sanskrit: gāṅgeyas tu raṇe pārtham ānarchan navabhiḥ śaraiḥ tam arjunaḥ pratyavidhyad daśabhir marmavedhibhiḥ
english: The son of Gaṅgā struck Pārtha in the battle with nine arrows, and Arjuna struck him back with ten that pierced the vitals.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasreṇa suprayuktena pāṇḍavaḥ arjunaḥ samaraślāghī bhīṣmasyāvārayad diśaḥ
english: Then, with a thousand well-aimed arrows, Arjuna the Pāṇḍava, glorious in battle, hemmed in all the quarters around Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: śarajālaṃ tatas tat tu śarajālena kaurava vārayām āsa pārthasya bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavas tathā
english: But that net of arrows, O Kaurava, Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu warded off in turn with his own net of arrows against Pārtha.

sanskrit: ubhau paramasaṃhṛṣṭāv ubhau yuddhābhinandinau nirviśeṣam ayudhyetāṃ kṛtapratikṛtaiṣiṇau
english: Both supremely exultant, both rejoicing in the battle, they fought as equals, each seeking to answer stroke with stroke.

sanskrit: bhīṣmacāpavimuktāni śarajālāni saṃghaśaḥ śīryamāṇāny adṛśyanta bhinnāny arjunasāyakaiḥ
english: The nets of arrows loosed from Bhīṣma's bow were seen breaking apart in masses, shattered by Arjuna's shafts.

sanskrit: tathaivārjunamuktāni śarajālāni bhāgaśaḥ gāṅgeyaśaranunnāni nyapatanta mahītale
english: And likewise the nets of arrows loosed by Arjuna, struck piecemeal by the son of Gaṅgā's shafts, fell down upon the earth.

sanskrit: arjunaḥ pañcaviṃśatyā bhīṣmam ārcchac chitaiḥ śaraiḥ bhīṣmo 'pi samare pārthaṃ vivyādha triṃśatā śaraiḥ
english: Arjuna struck Bhīṣma with twenty-five sharp arrows, and Bhīṣma too, in the battle, pierced Pārtha with thirty arrows.
